# Kyoto 5-Day Trip Plan: 10–14 April 2026

A balanced Kyoto itinerary for 2 adults with **temples, local food, and one slow afternoon**, keeping walking moderate and **no starts before 09:00**. Budget target is **180,000 JPY excluding flights**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Timeline

### Day 1: Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- 09:30: Check in / drop bags, then start with a gentle walk through **Gion** and **Sannenzaka**.
- 12:00: Lunch in Higashiyama with easy vegetarian options around temple streets.
- 14:00: Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** and nearby viewpoints at a relaxed pace.
- 18:00: Early dinner in central Kyoto; keep the evening light with a riverside stroll.

### Day 2: Arashiyama Temple and Bamboo Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- 09:30: Head to **Arashiyama** after the rush.
- 11:00: Walk the **Bamboo Grove** and visit **Tenryu-ji**.
- 13:00: Lunch near the river; look for tofu, yuba, or soba.
- 15:00: Optional short boat ride or café break; avoid packing too much into the afternoon.
- 18:30: Dinner back in central Kyoto.

### Day 3: Northern Kyoto Temples
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- 09:30: Start with **Kinkaku-ji** for a calm morning visit.
- 11:30: Continue to **Ryoan-ji** for the rock garden.
- 13:00: Lunch nearby with a vegetarian-friendly set meal.
- 14:30: Slow transfer to **Ninna-ji** or return to the hotel for rest.
- 19:00: Dinner in the city center, ideally near Nishiki or Kawaramachi.

### Day 4: Relaxing Kyoto Afternoon
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- 09:30: Visit **Nishiki Market** for a late breakfast-style food walk.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=09:30: Visit **Nishiki Market** for a late breakfast-style food walk, Kyoto, Japan
- 11:30: Light temple stop or shopping in the surrounding arcade streets.
- 13:30: **Relaxing afternoon**: tea house, spa, or quiet café time with minimal walking.
- 17:00: Optional sunset river walk along the Kamo River.
- 19:00: Dinner with a focus on vegetarian-friendly Kyoto cuisine.

### Day 5: East Kyoto Farewell
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- 09:30: Easy morning at **Philosopher’s Path** or one final temple visit.
Media: Alt=09:30: Easy morning at **Philosopher’s Path** or one final temple visit, Kyoto, Japan
- 11:30: Coffee and souvenir stop in Okazaki or Higashiyama.
- 13:00: Farewell lunch with a tofu or soba focus.
- 15:00: Return to hotel, collect luggage, and depart at a relaxed pace.

## Budget Breakdown and Spending Plan

| Category | Planned Spend | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Accommodation | 70,000 JPY | 4 nights, mid-range hotel or ryokan-style stay |
| Food & drinks | 44,000 JPY | About 5,500 JPY per person per day |
| Local transport | 12,000 JPY | Subway, buses, taxis for convenience |
| Temple admissions | 8,000 JPY | Kiyomizu-dera, Kinkaku-ji area, Tenryu-ji, others |
| Relaxing afternoon / tea / spa | 10,000 JPY | One slower, comfort-focused day block |
| Snacks, coffee, extras | 16,000 JPY | Nishiki Market, desserts, small purchases |
| Contingency | 20,000 JPY | Buffer for taxis, upgrades, or extra meals |

**Total: 180,000 JPY**

## Map-Style Kyoto Activity Areas

### Higashiyama
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- **Best for:** Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Gion
- **Why go:** Classic Kyoto streets, temple views, easy half-day walking
- **Food:** Yuba, tofu sets, matcha sweets

### Arashiyama
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Best for:** Bamboo Grove, Tenryu-ji, river views
- **Why go:** Scenic but manageable if you keep it to one main area
- **Food:** Soba, tofu, light café lunch

### Northern Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Best for:** Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji, Ninna-ji
- **Why go:** Strong temple day with straightforward transfers
- **Food:** Simple set meals, vegetarian temple-style dishes

### Central Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Best for:** Nishiki Market, Kawaramachi, Kamo River
- **Why go:** Good for food, shopping, and easy evenings
- **Food:** Market snacks, tofu, desserts, coffee

### Okazaki / Philosopher’s Path
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- **Best for:** Gentle walking, quieter temple stops, tea breaks
- **Why go:** Best fit for a slower, restorative day
- **Food:** Café brunch, tea, light vegetarian lunch

## Best-Fit Trip Notes

- **Moderate walking:** Group temples by area and use taxis for one or two short hops.
- **Vegetarian traveler:** Kyoto is a strong fit for tofu, yuba, soba, and shojin ryori.
- **No early starts:** This plan keeps every day starting around **09:30**.
- **Pace:** Two fuller temple days, two mixed food/culture days, and one clearly slower afternoon.

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Plan Hotels] https://www.booking.com/city/jp/kyoto.html
Action: [Button: Check Trains] https://www.japanrailpass-reservation.net/
Action: [Button: Temple Info] https://www.kyototemple.com/

## Sources
- Kyoto tourism overview: https://kyoto.travel/en
- Kyoto temple and area reference: https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2158.html
- Transit planning: https://www.google.com/maps/
